subject: community-medicine
title: National Immunisation Schedule: Vaccines and Protection Timeline

steps.title: Birth doses: immediate newborn protection
steps.tx: The Universal Immunisation Programme mandates three **birth doses** before hospital discharge: BCG at 0.05 ml intradermally over the left deltoid, bivalent oral polio vaccine zero dose at two drops orally, and hepatitis B birth dose at 0.5 ml intramuscularly within 24 hours of delivery. Hepatitis B birth dose prevents perinatal vertical transmission from chronic carrier mothers and must not be delayed beyond 24 hours.
steps.say: Give BCG, oral polio zero dose and hepatitis B within 24 hours of birth. The hepatitis B shot prevents vertical transmission and loses its protective window if given late.

steps.tx: The pale bleb on the left deltoid is the correct end point of intradermal BCG. The programme mandates three **birth doses** before hospital discharge. BCG is 0.05 ml intradermally over the left deltoid, bivalent oral polio vaccine is a zero dose of two drops by mouth, and hepatitis B is 0.5 ml intramuscularly within 24 hours of delivery. That hepatitis B dose blocks perinatal spread from a carrier mother and loses its window if delayed past 24 hours.
steps.say: BCG should raise a bleb in the skin of the left deltoid before the infant leaves hospital. The same birth package adds two drops of oral polio vaccine and an intramuscular hepatitis B dose within 24 hours. Given later, hepatitis B misses the chance to block spread from a carrier mother.

vis.alt: A pale bleb rises on an infant left deltoid as BCG vaccine is injected into the skin.
vis.caption: Intradermal BCG on the left deltoid lifts a pale bleb, the sign that the birth dose has entered the skin. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Primary infant series at six, ten, and fourteen weeks
steps.tx: The **primary infant series** begins at six weeks, repeating at ten and fourteen weeks, delivering pentavalent vaccine containing diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B and Haemophilus influenzae type b, along with bivalent OPV drops and liquid rotavirus vaccine. Fractional inactivated polio vaccine is co-administered as two 0.1 ml intradermal doses at six and fourteen weeks on the right deltoid to establish mucosal and systemic immunity.
steps.say: At six, ten and fourteen weeks, infants receive pentavalent, oral polio drops and rotavirus vaccine. Fractional inactivated polio is injected intradermally at six and fourteen weeks.

steps.title: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine schedule
steps.tx: The **pneumococcal conjugate vaccine** schedule follows a two plus one regimen under the national schedule, administered as two primary doses at six weeks and fourteen weeks, followed by a booster dose at nine completed months. Injection is delivered intramuscularly into the anterolateral aspect of the mid-thigh, preventing invasive pneumococcal disease including bacteraemic pneumonia and bacterial meningitis in infants under two years.
steps.say: Pneumococcal vaccine follows a two plus one schedule: primary shots at six and fourteen weeks, followed by a booster at nine completed months.

steps.title: Nine-month transition and Japanese encephalitis
steps.tx: At nine completed months, the infant receives the first dose of **measles rubella vaccine** subcutaneous at 0.5 ml on the right upper arm, alongside the first dose of vitamin A oral suspension at 100,000 international units. In endemic districts, the live attenuated SA 14-14-2 Japanese encephalitis vaccine first dose is administered subcutaneously in the left upper arm, while PCV booster is given concurrently.
steps.say: Nine months marks the transition to measles rubella, the first dose of vitamin A, the PCV booster, and Japanese encephalitis vaccine in endemic districts.

steps.tx: At nine completed months the infant receives oral vitamin A and the first measles rubella injection together. The **measles rubella vaccine** is 0.5 ml given subcutaneously on the right upper arm, and the first vitamin A dose is 100,000 international units by mouth. In endemic districts live attenuated SA 14 14 2 Japanese encephalitis vaccine is given subcutaneously in the left upper arm. The pneumococcal conjugate booster is given at the same visit.
steps.say: Nine months brings the first measles rubella injection, 0.5 ml under the skin of the right upper arm, plus 100,000 units of vitamin A by mouth. Endemic districts add Japanese encephalitis vaccine in the left upper arm. The pneumococcal booster is due at that same visit.

vis.alt: An infant at nine months receives oral vitamin A syrup and a subcutaneous measles rubella injection.
vis.caption: At nine months the infant is given vitamin A by mouth and the measles rubella vaccine under the skin of the upper arm. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Second year boosters and vitamin A schedule
steps.tx: Between sixteen and twenty-four months, children receive **second year boosters** consisting of the DPT first booster intramuscularly, the second dose of measles rubella vaccine subcutaneously, the second Japanese encephalitis dose where applicable, and an OPV booster dose. Vitamin A prophylaxis continues with 200,000 international units every six months until five years of age, completing a total of nine doses across childhood.
steps.say: Between sixteen and twenty-four months, give DPT first booster, MR second dose, OPV booster and Japanese encephalitis second dose. Vitamin A continues biannually.

nodes.label: Vitamin A every 6 months to 5 years

steps.title: School age boosters and tetanus-diphtheria replacement
steps.tx: At five to six years, children receive the second DPT booster to renew waning pertussis and diphtheria protection before primary school entry. National policy replaced tetanus toxoid with **tetanus and adult diphtheria vaccine** for adolescents at ten years and sixteen years, as well as for pregnant women, ensuring sustained community immunity against adult diphtheria outbreaks while preserving neonatal tetanus elimination gains.
steps.say: The second DPT booster arrives at five years. At ten and sixteen years, Td vaccine replaces tetanus toxoid to prevent adult diphtheria outbreaks.

steps.title: Closing coverage gaps with Mission Indradhanush
steps.tx: The government launched **Mission Indradhanush** and its intensified phases to rapidly accelerate full immunisation coverage in low-performing districts, urban slums, remote hamlets and nomadic settlements. By head-counting dropouts and left-out infants through door-to-door microplanning, mobile vaccination teams conduct multi-day focused immunization drives each month to deliver missed antigens, reducing infant morbidity in vulnerable geographic pockets.
steps.say: Mission Indradhanush targets geographic pockets where routine sessions miss children. Mobile teams conduct intensive monthly rounds to find dropouts and administer overdue doses.

steps.title: Digital tracking through the U-WIN portal
steps.tx: The **U-WIN platform** digitises the entire maternal and child immunisation registry across public and private sectors in India, creating individual beneficiary records linked to unique registration identifiers. It automates automated SMS vaccination alerts, generates session lists for auxiliary nurse midwives, verifies digital certificates with QR codes, and tracks individual children across district boundaries to minimise dropouts.
steps.say: The U-WIN platform registers every pregnant mother and newborn child. It sends automated reminder texts, creates session lists, and prevents dropouts during migration.

steps.title: Catch-up vaccination and zero dose children
steps.tx: Children who have received no routine vaccinations are classified as **zero dose children**, demanding prompt catch-up according to national guidelines without restarting the series. Pentavalent and rotavirus vaccines can be initiated up to one year of age, while DPT boosters can be given up to seven years. When an older child presents late, health workers administer all eligible missed antigens simultaneously at distinct anatomical sites.
steps.say: For children presenting late, never restart an interrupted vaccination series. Administer all overdue eligible vaccines at separate anatomical sites during the same visit.

rows: Give 0.1 ml if over 1 month old
Administer Td if older than 7 years
